children: A sustained gold rebound likely requires an unwinding of Fed tightening expectations and improved risk sentiment, says Pepperstone's Dilin Wu. The precious metal hasn't performed as one might expect amid risk-off sentiment. Rather than spurring safe-haven flows into gold, Wu thinks the selloff in U.S. equities may have prompted some investors to liquidate gold positions to cover losses or meet margin calls elsewhere. Gold also hasn't benefited from haven flows into U.S. Treasurys driving yields lower, suggesting that liquidity pressures and position unwinding may be outweighing the tailwind. A decisive break below $4,000/oz could trigger further long liquidation. To signal recovery, gold needs to reclaim $4,100-$4,110 an ounce, Wu says. Gold traded last at $4,012 an ounce after briefly falling to $3,986 an ounce. (fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)
